requirements.text: Keep the existing stack: Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router.
Use plain CSS with the design-token theme.
Use system fonts only.
Every page is prerendered to its own HTML file.
Every prerendered page has its own title.
Every prerendered page has its own meta description.
Every prerendered page has its own Open Graph tags.
Every prerendered page has its own canonical link.
The training filter remains hydrated and working.
The Menu button remains hydrated and working.
The contact form remains hydrated and working.
No backend, analytics, third-party scripts or external CDNs.
Existing acceptance tests keep passing except where this task changes that behavior.

Brand colors: deep navy #0B1F3A, white, and teal #1F8A8A as the one accent; darker navy #071528 for premium bands, pale teal-grey #F2F7F7 for alternate section backgrounds, hairline #E3E8EF for borders.
Headings use a Georgia-style system serif font.
Body text uses a sans-serif font.
System monospace (ui-monospace) is used only for small technical labels: diagram labels, eyebrow tags and deliverable names.
WCAG AA contrast everywhere, including text over photos and on the diagrams.
Subtle motion only: fade/slide-in of sections and hover lifts.
All motion is turned off under prefers-reduced-motion.
Hero h1 is 60-64px on desktop (1440px).
Hero h1 is 38-40px on phones (390px).
Section h2 is 40-44px on desktop.
Section h2 is 28-32px on phones.
Body text is 17-18px with line-height 1.6.
Every section has a small uppercase teal eyebrow label above its h2 (e.g. "WHO WE SERVE", "WHAT WE BUILD").
Content max width is 1200px, centered.
Section padding is 96px top and bottom on desktop.
Section padding is 64px top and bottom on phones.
An 8px spacing scale is used throughout.
No horizontal scrolling at 390px width.
Section backgrounds alternate white, pale teal-grey and navy.
Home has at least three navy bands (systems, testimonial, call to action).
Home never has two plain white sections of card grids in a row.
Wherever a photo sits beside text on desktop, the text column holds a heading, a paragraph and at least one supporting element (list, link or meta line).
Cards have a 12px radius and a 1px #E3E8EF border.
Cards have a soft shadow that lifts slightly on hover.
Every card icon sits in a 44px pale-teal rounded-square tile, not bare on the card.
Diagrams are inline SVG using a viewBox with no fixed pixel widths, so they scale with the page.
Diagram labels are real <text> elements in the monospace font.
Diagrams have a title and desc for screen readers.
On phones a wide diagram may stack vertically but its labels stay readable (at least 12px).

Use only the existing photos in public/images/ (hero-boardroom, smb-owner, team-workshop, enterprise-atrium, custom-development, strategy-session, about-office, contact-meeting, each as NAME.jpg and NAME-768.jpg); do not generate or download images.
Photos are rendered with (or ) with a srcset including the 768w and 1344w versions.
Photos have a sizes attribute.
Photos have width and height attributes.
Photos use loading="lazy" except the hero photo.
Photos use decoding="async".
Photos have descriptive alt text.
Photos are never captioned or presented as the firm's own team or clients.
Where text sits on a photo, a navy gradient overlay is placed behind the text so it meets WCAG AA.
Illustrations are inline SVG in the brand colors, with no image files.
Every service item has a line icon.
Every training format has a line icon.
Every engagement tier has a line icon.
Every systems capability has a line icon.
Every deliverable has a line icon.
Icons are drawn in one consistent style on a 24px grid with 1.5-2px strokes.
A subtle background motif of overlapping bell curves or a fine data-grid pattern appears behind the hero.
A subtle background motif of overlapping bell curves or a fine data-grid pattern appears behind the navy bands.
The architecture diagram is one React component used on the Systems page and in the Home systems band.
Architecture diagram top row is labeled "Your systems" and contains "CRM", "ERP", "Data warehouse" and "Documents".
Architecture diagram middle row is labeled "Agent orchestration" and contains "Planner", "Tool-using agents" and "Human approval".
Architecture diagram has "Models (vendor-neutral)" beside the orchestration row.

Architecture diagram uses white and teal on navy backgrounds.

Professional services example "Agentic document intake" with the specified challenge (documents by email in many formats keyed in by hand), system (agents classify and extract into the practice-management system with a person approving anything uncertain), and observed and sustained (every document traced end to end, accuracy evaluation set, weekly review queue).

Manufacturing example "Connected maintenance forecasting" with the specified challenge (sensor data, maintenance system and ERP never talk), system (forecasting pipeline joining all three and scheduling maintenance work orders), and observed and sustained (data-quality and drift monitors, retraining runbooks, an owner on the client's team).

Retail example "Customer service copilot" with the specified challenge (staff search several systems per question), system (retrieval-augmented assistant over product catalog, order system and policies that drafts answers for staff), and observed and sustained (answer-quality evaluations, cost per conversation tracked, guardrails reviewed monthly).

Systems section id "architecture" with h2 "Multi-system architecture" lists: integration with CRM, ERP, data warehouses and document stores; event-driven and API-based designs; data contracts between systems; security reviews and least-privilege access.
